title: crash: ArgumentOutOfRangeException in ParseTfms when discovering real .NET repos
description:
## Symptom

When running `testaruda-adapter-dotnet` (via `titi testaruda-adapter`) against real-world .NET repos, the `discover` command crashes with an `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` during TFM (Target Framework Moniker) parsing.

## Stack trace

```
Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Specified argument was out of the range of valid values. (Parameter 'start')
   at titi.Interop.MsBuildSetup.<>c.<ParseTfms>b__10_0(String tfm) in /src/titi/Interop.cs:line 138
   at System.Linq.Enumerable.SizeOptIListSelectIterator`2.MoveNext()
   at System.Linq.Enumerable.<ToArray>g__EnumerableToArray|324_0[TSource](IEnumerable`1 source)
   at titi.Interop.MsBuildSetup.ParseTfms(String raw) in /src/titi/Interop.cs:line 132
   at titi.Interop.MsBuildSetup.ConvertNode(ProjectGraphNode node) in /src/titi/Interop.cs:line 65
   at titi.Core.Program.BuildGraphForRepo() in /src/titi/Core.cs:line 85
   at titi.Core.Program.TestarudaAdapterCommand() in /src/titi/Core.cs:line 963
```

## Root cause

`titi/Interop.cs:138` in `ParseTfms()` — the `String.Substring(start)` call uses a `start` index that exceeds the string length. This happens when parsing certain TFM formats from real csproj files.

The current implementation likely assumes a fixed format (e.g., `"net10.0"`) but real repos may use multi-targeting (`<TargetFrameworks>net9.0;net10.0</TargetFrameworks>`), complex monikers, or platform-specific suffixes.

## Repros on

All 10 real-world .NET repos tested crash with this same error:
- AutoMapper/AutoMapper, NLog/NLog, serilog/serilog, FluentValidation/FluentValidation, restsharp/RestSharp, xunit/xunit, nunit/nunit, App-vNext/Polly, dotnet/efcore, dotnet/maui

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/serilog/serilog /tmp/serilog
cd /tmp/serilog
echo '{"command":"discover","params":{}}' | titi testaruda-adapter
# Crashes with ArgumentOutOfRangeException
```

## Expected behavior

- Discover handles any valid .NET TFM format without crashing
- Unknown or unparseable TFMs are gracefully skipped with a warning
- At least 5 real .NET repos can complete the discover phase

## Workaround

None — the adapter is currently unusable for real-world stress-testing.

## Traceability

Discovered during testaruda stress-test-10x .NET verification (testaruda-6c6.9, testaruda-6c6.10). Blocks testaruda from reaching 10 .NET repos.
close_reason: Completed: ParseTfms no longer crashes on trailing semicolons, whitespace-only segments, platform suffixes, or short monikers. 16 tests covering all edge cases added. Verified against 6 real-world .NET repos (Serilog, FluentValidation, NLog, Polly, xunit, AutoMapper) — all complete discover without crash. All 242 tests pass. Commit 9f6372c pushed to main.

title: S4: Resolve InTitiContext contradiction between RS-04 and SG-04
description:
Cross-capability contradiction between RS-04 and SG-04:

- solution-generation SG-04: unconditionally states that generated solution includes InTitiContext=true for all builds initiated from the transient solution
- reference-swap RS-04: states that when no swaps occur, SwapResult.msbuildContext has inTitiContext=false

SG-04's globalProperties are meant to flow from SwapResult.msbuildContext — the exact object RS-04 describes. So for 'titi open' on a project whose dependencies have no local source available (a plausible ordinary case), SG-04 requires InTitiContext=true while RS-04 requires false.

Add a conditional to one of these, or define the relationship precisely enough to show which wins.
close_reason: Fixed: SG-04 now conditional on swap result, with two scenarios matching RS-04's contract

title: S2: Fix CLI-08 TFM compatibility rule — non-empty intersection is wrong; should be superset
description:
In CLI-08 (cli/spec.md) the requirement states: '(2) its target framework set has a non-empty intersection with each consumer's target framework set.'

This is incorrect. A consumer that multi-targets net8.0;net9.0 needs the referenced project to support BOTH TFMs — if the candidate only supports net9.0, MSBuild will fail on the consumer's net8.0 leg. The correct rule is that the candidate's TFM set must be a SUPERSET of the consumer's TFM set.

This also affects reference-swap RS-01 which references the same compatibility concept but never states its own algorithm.
close_reason: Fixed: CLI-08 TFM rule now uses 'superset' instead of 'non-empty intersection'

title: S3: Specify versionPolicy=FORCE — declared in RS-01 and CF-02 but has no defined behaviour
description:
versionPolicy=FORCE is declared in RS-01 (reference-swap/spec.md) and CF-02 (configuration/spec.md) as a valid value alongside STRICT and SEMVER_COMPATIBLE, but has ZERO requirements or scenarios anywhere in the nine spec files.

An implementer has a named, user-facing policy value with no defined behaviour. We need to decide:
- Which safety checks does FORCE bypass? (version, TFM, cycle, transitive floor?)
- How does it interact with the overrides bypass set that RS-01 defines for the same purpose?
- Document the behaviour with scenarios.
close_reason: Fixed: FORCE policy behavior defined in RS-01 (bypasses all safety checks except NO_LOCAL_SOURCE) with two scenarios

title: S1: Fix DG-04 Completeness invariant direction — the formal invariant asserts the wrong reachability direction
description:
In dependency-graph/spec.md, DG-04 states: 'For every project P in the graph, if P is reachable via dependency edges from any project in directlyAffected, then P SHALL appear in either directlyAffected or transitivelyAffected.'

This is backwards. Dependency edges go from a project TO its dependencies. So 'reachable via dependency edges from X' means X's upstream dependencies. But transitivelyAffected contains downstream DEPENDENTS of directlyAffected projects.

The invariant should say: 'if P is reachable from a directly affected project by following dependency edges in reverse (i.e. P is a transitive dependent of a directly affected project), then P SHALL appear in either directlyAffected or transitivelyAffected.'

The clarifying sentence 'No downstream dependent...' was added post-review but the formal invariant text itself is still provably wrong against the spec's own DG-02 worked example.
close_reason: Fixed: DG-04 Completeness invariant now uses correct direction (reachable by following dependency edges in reverse)

title: Add pure static dependency edge analysis
description:
## Problem

The static-deps handler (`HandleStaticDeps` in Adapter.cs) loads edges from cache (`.titi/test-cache/edges.json`), but these edges are only produced by `EdgeBuilder.BuildFromRun` which requires **coverage data** (TRX + Cobertura XML from a prior test run). Without a prior test run, the edge cache is empty and static-deps returns 0 edges.

This means titi, like Testimonial.jl, cannot do test selection on the first run — it falls back to "run all tests."

## What to build

Add a **pure static analysis pass** that produces test→source edges without running tests. Three levels of analysis:

**Level 1 — Project references (highest impact, lowest complexity):**
- Parse `.csproj` project references (`<ProjectReference>` elements)
- For each test project, find all source projects it references
- Emit edges: every test item in a test project → every source file in each referenced source project
- This is an over-approximation but safe (SAFE-001)

**Level 2 — Using statement analysis (medium complexity):**
- Scan test source files for `using Namespace;` statements
- Build a namespace→file map from source projects
- Match test file `using`s against source project namespaces
- Emit edges: specific test files → specific source files that match

**Level 3 — Method-level call graph (high complexity, stretch):**
- Parse method calls in test code (via Roslyn or regex) to find direct calls to source methods
- Map calls back to source files for precise edges

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Level 1 implemented: test project→source project edges via `.csproj` `<ProjectReference>`
- [ ] Level 2 implemented: `using` statement analysis produces file-level edges
- [ ] Unit tests for StaticEdgeAnalyzer with synthetic project structures (single project, multi-project, no test project)
- [ ] Static edges are persisted in the edge cache alongside coverage edges
- [ ] `HandleStaticDeps` falls back to static edges when no coverage edges exist
- [ ] Stress-test against 10 .NET repos shows >0 edges for at least 7/10 (without prior coverage)

## Cross-repo coordination

Review Testimonial.jl's StaticProvider interface (`testimonial-7e9x`) before finalizing the titi implementation, to ensure protocol-level consistency between the two static analysis approaches.

## Files
- `src/titi/EdgeBuilder.cs` or new `src/titi/StaticEdgeAnalyzer.cs`
- `src/titi/Adapter.cs` (HandleStaticDeps — use static edges as fallback)
- `src/titi/Safety.cs` (ComputeSelectedTests must handle static edges correctly)

## Related
- Testimonial.jl has the same gap: StaticLayer.jl exists but is not wired into the protocol. Tickets: testimonial-7e9x, testimonial-o410

title: fix(adapter): detect test projects by package references, not just IsTestProject flag
description:
titi's ConvertNode (Interop.cs) detects test projects using the MSBuild `IsTestProject` property. Most real-world .NET repos (AutoMapper, FluentValidation, etc.) don't set this property — they just reference test SDKs (xunit, NUnit, MSTest) via PackageReference.

**Impact:** The adapter always returns 0 tests for repos that don't explicitly set `<IsTestProject>true</IsTestProject>` in their .csproj. Even with source-roots fix (titi-9tg) and cold-cache warmup (titi-ua5), discover returns empty.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] `ConvertNode` SHALL detect test projects by checking PackageReferences for well-known test SDKs (xunit, NUnit, MSTest, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk) in addition to the `IsTestProject` MSBuild property
- [ ] Existing `IsTestProject` check continues to override (explicit wins over heuristics)
- [ ] Configurable list of test-SDK package IDs (optional override in titi.config.json)
- [ ] The default list SHALL include at least: xunit, NUnit, NUnit3TestAdapter, MSTest.TestAdapter, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestPlatform.TestFramework

**Why now:** All 9 .NET stress-test repos return 0 tests because none set IsTestProject=true.

title: fix(adapter): warm test cache on first discover invocation
description:
titi's adapter (Adapter.cs) calls DiscoverAllTestItems which relies on DiscoveryCache.GetOrDiscover. In the adapter subprocess context, the discovery callback returns an empty array (`=> []`) instead of running `dotnet test --list-tests`, because that's an interactive operation that can take minutes.

**Impact:** The testaruda adapter always returns `result: []` from discover on cold cache. The cache can only be pre-warmed by running `titi tests list <csproj>` separately, which isn't practical for the adapter workflow.



**Acceptance:**
- [ ] On first discover (cold cache), the adapter SHALL run `dotnet test --list-tests` for each test project
- [ ] Results SHALL be cached in the test-cache directory so subsequent invocations are fast
- [ ] Cache SHALL be invalidated when project files change (fingerprint comparison, already implemented in DiscoveryCache)
- [ ] Existing `titi tests list` flow continues to work (it already warms the cache)
- [ ] Adapter SHALL handle `dotnet test --list-tests` failures gracefully (repo has build errors) and return empty results for that project

**Why now:** The adapter needs to work on first invocation for testaruda stress-testing. Without this, discover always returns 0 tests on cold cache, making the adapter unusable for the standard stress-test flow.
close_reason: Implemented in 82e419d: adapter now runs dotnet test --list-tests per test project on cold cache, parses output via TestDiscovery.Parser, caches results. Failures handled gracefully.

title: Migrate config and cache files from EDN to JSON
description:
The project originally planned ClojureCLR as the runtime, which motivated the EDN (.edn) config format and cache serialization. The actual implementation is in C# with a hand-rolled regex parser that doesn't parse EDN properly, and cache files (edges.edn, history.edn) are already serialized as JSON. Switch to JSON for consistency, better tooling support, and a standard .NET format.

Changes:
- Config: replace custom regex EDN parser with System.Text.Json, rename titi.config.edn → titi.config.json
- Cache files: rename edges.edn → edges.json, history.edn → history.json, fingerprint.edn → fingerprint.json
- Source code: update all file path constants and references
- Tests: update file names and EDN syntax to JSON
- Docs/specs: update all .edn references to .json
close_reason: Completed: Config migrated from EDN to JSON format. Config.cs now uses System.Text.Json. Cache files (edges, history) renamed .edn → .json. Fixture config files updated. Docs/specs updated.

title: TitiOpen integration test is fragile to source-introduced build warnings
description:
The TitiOpen_AgainstFixture_GeneratesSlnx integration test spawns 'dotnet run --project titi.csproj -- open ...' (Debug, no --no-build). When any titi source change introduces a build warning, 'dotnet run' prints the warning to STDOUT, prefixing the JSON output (e.g. with the warning's file path '/var/home/...') and breaking JSON deserialization (System.Text.Json.JsonException: '/' is an invalid start of a value). This made CI red on f91c950 when a dropped null check produced CS8602. Reproduced locally: full Release suite was flaky (3/5 red) and 'dotnet run' stdout started with the warning line instead of '{'. The empty-vs-failure logic was correct; the test's coupling to warning-free stdout was the fragility.

ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
RED: with a deliberately-introduced CS8602 (or any warning) in titi source, TitiOpen_AgainstFixture_GeneratesSlnx fails with a JSON parse error (current behavior).
GREEN: the test still passes with a source warning present. Preferred fix — spawn the pre-built Release binary directly (the CI 'Build' step already produces it) OR use 'dotnet run --no-build --configuration Release', and assert stdout parses as JSON before deserializing so a non-JSON prefix produces a clear failure message. Other integration tests spawning 'dotnet run' (TitiClean) should be aligned if they share the pattern.
REFACTOR: extract a shared helper for 'run titi CLI and parse JSON stdout' so the no-build + JSON-validation discipline is applied consistently.
close_reason: Completed: extracted TitiTestRunner shared helper that invokes pre-built binary directly (no 'dotnet run'), validates JSON prefix on stdout. Both integration tests updated. All 277 tests pass, 6 skipped. Commit bc6ec50.

title: Remove nonexistent cache-warm guidance from adapter documentation

title: Comply with canonical testaruda adapter discover response format
description:
**Context**: titi's testaruda adapter returns discover items in a format that doesn't match the canonical testaruda adapter protocol (TIA-ADAPT-004).

**Current titi response**:
```json
{"ok":true,"result":{"tests":[{"test_id":"...","assembly_path":"...","class_name":"...","method_name":"...","framework":"...","tier":"..."}]}}
```

**Canonical format** (testaruda expects):
```json
{"ok":true,"result":[{"node_id":"...","suite_kind":"...","file":"..."}]}
```

**Issues**:
1. Envelope: canonical has `result` as a direct array; titi wraps in `result.tests`
2. Fields: canonical uses `node_id`, `suite_kind`, `file`; titi uses `test_id`, `assembly_path`, `class_name`, `method_name`, `framework`, `tier`

**Impact**: `AdapterIO::discover()` in testaruda cannot deserialize titi's discover response. The existing test (`titi_adapter_handshake_then_discover`) checks raw JSON, not the typed path.

**Fix approach**: Update `FormatResponse(AdapterTestItem[])` in `src/titi/Adapter.cs` to output the canonical format:
- Map `test_id` → `node_id`
- Map `class_name + method_name` → `suite_kind` (e.g. "ClassName.MethodName")
- Map `assembly_path` → `file`
- Output `result` as direct array, not `result.tests`

Alternatively, if method-level discovery with richer fields is desired, open a protocol version negotiation (bump to v2).
close_reason: Changed FormatResponse(AdapterTestItem[]) to output canonical testaruda format: result is a direct array, fields map to node_id/suite_kind/file. Updated unit and integration tests to match. Updated docs/adapter.md example.
